name: Renewable interconnection queue intelligence
demand: No verified search volume, installs, paying users, or reachable-buyer count surfaced. Scale proxies only: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory reports about 8,200 active U.S. transmission-queue projects at end-2025; separately, FeederIQ claims 8,492 Xcel DER applications across Minnesota and Colorado as of June 2026. These are different queue populations, and applications are not buyers. Sources: https://emp.lbl.gov/queues ; https://feederiq.com/press/
prices: FeederIQ Pro is listed at $99/month for queue search, feeder constraints, monthly diffs and exports: https://feederiq.com/upgrade . USTA lists a $175/month weekly change feed for CAISO, SPP, ISO-NE and NYISO: https://ustechautomations.com/resources/blog/us-interconnection-queue-index-july-2026 . Grid Status offers a free tier; its queue application is presented as Enterprise, with no public price: https://www.gridstatus.io/pricing . Xcel provides a free hosting-capacity map and lists a $300 pre-application report: https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer
copy_speed: Competitive pressure is real. MeanderX was already operating before this period and was reported available in Xcel territory by 26 May 2026; its product maps distribution feeders, hosting capacity and queue movement across utilities: https://now.solar/2026/05/27/this-ai-tool-helps-community-solar-developers-connect-to-the-grid-sooner-canary-media/ . USTA’s broader queue index launched 9 July 2026, with a paid weekly archive: https://ustechautomations.com/resources/blog/us-interconnection-queue-index-july-2026 . Grid Status released its multi-market queue application on 4 February 2026, before the requested window: https://docs.gridstatus.io/changelog/february-2026/4-february-release-interconnection-queues-application . I found no dated second launch of a directly matched feeder-level product since April; MeanderX’s Xcel coverage is already a direct substitute there.
platform_risk: High data-source dependence, low app-platform dependence. Xcel says its DER queue is updated monthly; its hosting-capacity map is a point-in-time high-level estimate, may omit newer queued projects, and is not a substitute for formal interconnection review. The product must avoid presenting screening estimates as guaranteed capacity or study outcomes: https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer . Confirm commercial reuse terms for each utility’s source data before selling derived feeds; public availability alone does not establish a redistribution licence.
defensible_asset: The qualifying moat is accumulated, normalized, versioned queue history joined to feeder constraints and validated source-specific interpretations. That can compound across monthly updates, but the underlying Xcel queue and map are public, and MeanderX already offers overlapping feeder-level intelligence in Xcel territory. FeederIQ offers CSV export, so strong switching costs are not evidenced; no network effect is evident. Medium moat only if the build establishes reliable history and coverage in underserved territories, rather than copying a single public dashboard. Sources: https://feederiq.com/upgrade ; https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer ; https://now.solar/2026/05/27/this-ai-tool-helps-community-solar-developers-connect-to-the-grid-sooner-canary-media/
build_effort: Medium-high for a trustworthy one-utility MVP: ingest and normalize source files, preserve snapshots, resolve project changes, join feeder constraints, generate diffs, and audit uncertain records before surfacing them. AI agents can handle routine parsing, coding, briefs and support triage, but source changes and misleading joins need human review. FeederIQ’s founder says he spent a year parsing Xcel disclosures; this is an unverified first-party complexity signal, not a build-time benchmark: https://feederiq.com/press/ . Avoid starting in Xcel territory without a differentiated wedge because MeanderX already covers it.
channel: Inbound-only: utility-specific SEO pages and free sample reports, public industry content, self-serve signup, contextual search ads, and opt-in partner or integration listings. Do not send cold email, SMS, DMs or calls. For UK marketing, the ICO says electronic marketing to individual subscribers, including sole traders, generally requires consent or a soft opt-in; its B2B guidance also notes UK GDPR applies when using personal data: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/ . Use public content and user-initiated signup as the default across markets, and check local advertising and privacy rules before running ads.
owner_hours_per_week: Estimated 4–5 hours/week once one territory’s pipeline is stable and self-serve; unverified. The initial build, data QA and onboarding another territory may exceed Ricardo’s 5-hour limit. Xcel’s monthly source cadence supports batching, but does not prove low maintenance: https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer
automation_reason: Estimate for a stable, single-territory operation, not measured performance. Agents could automate scheduled ingestion, change detection, report drafts, billing and routine support; human time remains for ambiguous source changes, validation, product decisions and inbound sales. FeederIQ describes monthly queue updates, diffs and self-serve subscription features, while Xcel’s source queue is monthly: https://feederiq.com/upgrade ; https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer
moat_assessment: Passes the required moat category only conditionally: a maintained, validated time-series dataset is a data moat, but public inputs and existing feeder-level competitors make a one-territory clone weak. Build the moat through reliable history, source-specific interpretation and underserved utility coverage. No network effect or meaningful switching cost is evidenced; CSV export makes portability easy. Sources: https://feederiq.com/upgrade ; https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer ; https://now.solar/2026/05/27/this-ai-tool-helps-community-solar-developers-connect-to-the-grid-sooner-canary-media/
desk_test: Within one day, use Xcel’s public queue and free map to produce one clearly labelled sample feeder page showing the source date, constraint context and a reproducible month-to-month change. Publish it with a transparent $99/month interest or pilot prompt, then distribute only through a public industry post or opt-in partner listing. Pass only if a developer independently asks for access or a paid pilot; do not contact named queue applicants. Sources: https://www.xcelenergy.com/working_with_us/how_to_interconnect/hosting_capacity_map_disclaimer ; https://feederiq.com/upgrade
red_flags: No verified revenue, churn, customer count or operator hours; the $99 price is an offer, not proof of payment. FeederIQ’s public pages also conflict on CHI311 figures: its press kit says about 36 years and 59% on hold, while its sample case describes 36 months and 67%; the sample page also says data is delivered daily while describing the queue as monthly. These may reflect different dates or definitions, but require raw-data and methodology checks. Sources: https://feederiq.com/press/ ; https://feederiq.com/sample ; https://feederiq.com/upgrade . MeanderX already overlaps Xcel territory, so a same-territory clone has a weak wedge: https://now.solar/2026/05/27/this-ai-tool-helps-community-solar-developers-connect-to-the-grid-sooner-canary-media/
